title: Heaps & Priority Queues
subtitle: A heap exposes the best current candidate without sorting every candidate, so the invariant is about the root rather than the whole array.
variables: n = input items, k = selection size/rank, u = distinct keys, r = input streams/lists, N = total merged items, V/E = vertices/edges, H = physical heap entries including stale records, a = live tasks, T = produced schedule length, B = payload/key size when relevant. Standard-library heapq is a min-heap on a list; max-heaps here use negative numeric keys for Python 3.10 compatibility. Comparisons/arithmetic use a fixed-word model; Python big integers cost by bit length. Hash operations are expected O(1), with O(B) initial hashing/comparison costs for long keys. Heap push/pop comparison work is logarithmic; Python list capacity growth/shrink makes allocation bounds amortized across operations (a resize may copy O(n) references). Auxiliary space excludes output unless stated; stale heap entries and sorted copies are included. Keys must be consistently ordered, with no NaN. Ties require explicit counters when payloads are unorderable.

O(log(a+2)) amortized edit/remove/pop; individual pop O((a+1) log(a+2)), rebuild O(a+1)
O(a+1) after compaction; O(a+1) temporary rebuild

Hashable stable keys; consistently comparable finite numeric priorities; arbitrary unorderable payloads. set inserts/replaces key, ties execute in most-recent set serial order; remove returns bool; pop returns (key,priority,payload), raises IndexError when no live items. New versions invalidate old entries by identity. With compaction H <= 2a+16 after edits, a single pop can drain O(a+1) stale entries at O(log(a+2)) each: O((a+1) log(a+2)) worst case. A threshold rebuild costs O(a+1), while set can cost O(a+1) on a rebuild and remove likewise. Amortized O(log(a+2)) bounds charge each stale extraction to the edit that created it and each rebuild to the many invalidations since the preceding rebuild; use the maximum live size across a sequence for a uniform sequence bound.
